column1: # BRANCH PROTECT LIST — hand-maintained. The ONLY hand-entered input to branch deletion.
# scripts/branch-cleanup.cjs derives everything else from git and the GitHub API: what is in
# main, what a pull ref holds, what the archive branch covers, what heads an open PR. This file
# answers the one question no machine in CI can:
#     IS SOMEONE STANDING ON THIS BRANCH RIGHT NOW?
# WHY IT CANNOT BE DERIVED. A GitHub Actions runner cannot read the Claude session API. A branch
# can be `in-main` — the safest bucket there is — and still be the outcome branch of a running
# session.
# HOW TO REFRESH, and it MUST be refreshed before any deletion run:
#   list_sessions -> session_context.outcomes[].git_repository.git_info.branches
#   NOT external_metadata.current_branches, which holds the REPO NAME. 46 sessions report
#   "barakatammre84/Homiquity" there and 14 report an empty string; reading the wrong field
#   returns a plausible list of nothing.
# TWO RULES THIS LIST FOLLOWS, both learned by getting them wrong on 2026-08-31:
#   1. ONLY BRANCHES THAT EXIST ON ORIGIN. The first version was written straight from
#      list_sessions without checking, and 7 of its 15 rows named branches that were not on
#      origin at all — four had NEVER been pushed. A row naming nothing protects nothing while
#      reading as protection, which is the config-key-matches-nothing shape (d390dcacf3fe,
#      95770d4e56a7). branch-cleanup.cjs WARNS on such a row rather than ignoring it.
#   2. ONLY SESSIONS ACTIVE WITHIN 7 DAYS. An IDLE session is not a working one; it is a session
#      that has not touched its branch since.
# Sessions whose status is ARCHIVED are never listed: an archived session is not coming back.
# ⚠️ A COUNT IS NOT EVIDENCE OF LIFE. The 2026-09-01 version kept feat/landing-coach-first on the
# strength of "14 sessions". Fifteen of those sixteen were already ARCHIVED — rule 3 above, not
# applied to the number that was doing the arguing. One non-archived session touched it, idle 6
# days then and 22 by 2026-09-16. Count the sessions that rule 3 admits, then apply rule 2.
# Read 2026-09-16T16:09Z · 45 sessions · 10 non-archived, of which EIGHT name a branch and
# exactly ONE of those branches exists on origin. The other seven were never pushed or were
# auto-deleted on merge — rule 1 drops them rather than letting them read as protection.
# branch
claude/eager-hamilton-8bd0mk
column4: PR #805 open and the session was active today. Belt-and-braces: branch-cleanup.cjs already refuses any open-PR head (rule 2 of five), so this row is a second lock on a door that is shut.
